findings.reason: the write path and placement both change (node.py to a module routing does not import, or a function-local import the plan must sanction), and under an exact-SPEC build a worker hitting the cycle must either deviate from the stated placement or block, so naming the correct home before dispatch removes the deviation.
findings.text: §16 places the one shared resolver in `reckon/crew/node.py` beside `repository_identity`, but the resolver must read `mounted_repository_projects` from `reckon/crew/routing.py` (`reckon/crew/routing.py:3241`), and `routing.py` already imports `reckon/crew/node.py` at module scope (`reckon/crew/routing.py:38`), so a module-level `node -> routing` import is a hard cycle that fails at import time; the home the plan names is not one the resolver can be written into without a deferred import, while `routing.py` itself is already imported by all three call sites (`reckon/crew_dispatch_commands.py:528`, `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:205`, `reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:52`)
